# Best portable power station for camping

The right size depends on your trip. Most reviewers say the 250-500Wh class is the sweet spot for tent camping, and you only need to go bigger for a fridge or multiple days off-grid.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 270-290Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249): PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4 and weighs 8.3 lb, which is enough for phones, lights and a CPAP for a few nights. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is mainly available through Amazon and other retailers. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299): 286Wh with a 600W inverter, double the Jackery's, and expandable to 572Wh. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199): 288Wh, a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard model with an AC outlet, not the "C300 DC." OutdoorGearLab scored it lower (50/100) in its own testing, so it's a value pick rather than a performance pick. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179): the budget option, with 268Wh and a 600W inverter. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Mid-size for a fridge, laptop or longer trips
- **Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale for under $530. It's compact at 25 lb and measured 890Wh usable. The downsides are a noisy fan and limited capacity. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti AC180** ($499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF): 1,152Wh, an 1,800W inverter, about 35 lb and a 5-year warranty. Dealectric tested the code in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. It has no expansion port. [Buy at Bluetti (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). Dealectric earns a commission on purchases, and the store's checkout has the final price. [Details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)

## Multi-day off-grid
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top camping pick (81/100), now under $900 on Amazon. It has 2,200W output and weighs 39 lb. It won't run a space heater or electric burner for long. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799): TechRadar's best for camping, and PowerStationGearLab's pick for van or overland use. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** ($1,079): WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65-rated and weighs about 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## My pick
For most campers, the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** or **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** is enough. If you want to run a cooler or fridge, go with the **Anker C1000 Gen 2** or **Bluetti AC180**.

## Tips
- Turn off your CPAP's humidifier, which can triple its power draw.
- A folding solar panel extends a trip.
- Black Friday sales are coming, so prices may drop soon. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
